newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban court jails rail workers for fatal crash.
newsitem.headline: Cuban court jails rail workers for fatal crash.

text.p: A Cuban court has jailed four railway workers for 11 years after finding them guilty of drunk driving and responsible for a train crash in February in which 18 people died and 68 were injured.

The court in Ciego de Avila, in central Cuba, sentenced the driver and three other train crew after convicting them on charges that included driving drunk and permitting drunk driving, the ruling Communist Party newspaper Granma reported on Tuesday.
Another rail worker was sentenced to seven years in jail and a nurse on duty at a railway medical post to three years.
The convicted workers were crewing a passenger train packed with young military conscripts travelling from the eastern city of Bayamo to Havana on Feb. 10.

It ran off the rails after slamming into a goods locomotive near the central town of Ciego de Avila, about 380 km (240 miles) southeast of Havana. State media said at the time it appeared the passenger train had ignored a signal.
